Sergey Brin’s Childhood Shaped His View Of The World
Speaking at Stanford University in December 2025, Brin was asked what "limiting beliefs" he had to overcome while building Google and how those beliefs influenced his decision-making.

Rather than pointing to one specific belief, Brin traced his answer back to his childhood in Moscow, then part of the Soviet Union. He described growing up in a small apartment with his parents and grandmother, recalling a time when "everybody was very poor."

Brin said he initially had little sense of what existed beyond his immediate surroundings. That changed after his father learned more about life in the West and eventually decided the family should move to the U.S.

children: Moving to America Forced Brin To Start Over
The transition was difficult. Brin had to learn a new language, make new friends and adjust to an unfamiliar country. His family also remained financially struggling after the move.
Still, Brin described the experience as challenging but "awakening," saying his life expanded dramatically at several stages.
"I guess those challenging transitions can pay off," Brin said.
Stanford Gave Google’s Co-Founder New Kind of Freedom

Brin experienced another major shift when he arrived at Stanford for graduate school in 1993. He said the freedom professors gave him, along with California’s culture, felt "freeing and liberating" and encouraged a broader way of thinking.
